Increase the carved margin to produce a usable ground court rather than a token subtraction.
Open the court to the access side so the mass responds clearly to the street edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the frontage-related public void into a legible usable court rather than a shallow cave, aligning the ground response with the neighborhood-living access brief.
Enlarge the carved court enough to be read as public space in plan and section.
Orient the public opening toward the verified access side so the ground threshold becomes legible and semantically aligned.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass across views: a compact stepped bar with a continuous bend, not a pile of unrelated fragments. The silhouette is legible and the mass retains hierarchy, but the public/ground response is weak; the road edge is acknowledged only indirectly and the carved void is too small to register as a meaningful neighborhood threshold. The section language is acceptable for a compact mixed-use block, but it still skews toward a sculpted object more than an actively occupied street building. Overall, it is program-plausible and repairable, with good continuity and no obvious cross-view collision, but it would benefit from a stronger carved access void or court on the frontage side.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped massing can still read as one dominant object when the taper is coherent and the silhouette is clean.

warnings: The public void is underdeveloped relative to the explicit active-edge brief.
Frontage response is semantically soft; the mass does not yet strongly open to the verified access edge.
Stepped profile is coherent, but currently reads more as formal modulation than as a program-driven section.
No hard rejection: containment and cross-view consistency appear acceptable.
